## Multipole family {#sec-elements-multipoles}

The OPALX `MULTIPOLE` element is a straight magnet with normal and skew
multipole terms from quadrupole to decapole. `QUADRUPOLE` uses the same
runtime element with only the quadrupole term. There is no separate
`SEXTUPOLE` element; a sextupole is a `MULTIPOLE` with only its order-2 entry
set.

### Field expansion and conventions

The field is
$$
B_y + i B_x = \sum_{m=0}^{4} (B_m - i A_m) (x + i y)^m,
$$
where:

- $m = 0$ is the dipole term, $m = 1$ the quadrupole, $m = 2$ the sextupole,
  $m = 3$ the octupole and $m = 4$ the decapole,
- $B_m$ are normal coefficients,
- $A_m$ are skew coefficients.

The class `Multipole` (`src/AbsBeamline/Multipole.h`) uses the same indexing:
`n = 0` is the dipole, `n = 1` the quadrupole, and so on up to
`MAX_MP_ORDER - 1 = 4`.

For the quadrupole and sextupole terms the transverse field is:

$$
\text{normal quadrupole:}\qquad
B_x = B_1\,y,\qquad
B_y = B_1\,x,
$$

$$
\text{skew quadrupole:}\qquad
B_x = -A_1\,x,\qquad
B_y = A_1\,y,
$$

$$
\text{normal sextupole:}\qquad
B_x = 2 B_2\,x y,\qquad
B_y = B_2 (x^2 - y^2),
$$

$$
\text{skew sextupole:}\qquad
B_x = -A_2 (x^2 - y^2),\qquad
B_y = 2 A_2\,x y.
$$

The same function, `Multipole::computeField`, evaluates the field for the
particles and for the reference particle, so both see all orders.

### `MULTIPOLE`

The parser-side element `OpalMultipole` (`src/Elements/OpalMultipole.cpp`)
accepts the coefficient arrays:

- `KN`: normal normalized strengths $K_n$, in $\mathrm m^{-(n+1)}$
- `DKN`: normal strength errors
- `KS`: skew normalized strengths
- `DKS`: skew strength errors

Each array may have at most five entries, and the first (dipole) entry of each
must be zero. `MULTIPOLE` is placed as a straight element, so a dipole term
would steer the beam away from it; use `SBEND` or `RBEND` instead.

At update time the strengths and their errors are added and converted to field
coefficients with the rigidity $P_0/c$ from the global `P0` (GeV/$c$, default
1):
$$
B_n = \frac{P_0}{c}\,\frac{K_n + \Delta K_n}{n!},
\qquad
A_n = \frac{P_0}{c}\,\frac{K_{s,n} + \Delta K_{s,n}}{n!}.
$$
The charge of the beam does not enter: a positive $K_1$ focuses positive
particles horizontally and defocuses negative ones.

`OpalMultipole` sets these coefficients on a `MultipoleRep`
(`src/BeamlineCore/MultipoleRep.h`), which also holds the element length in
its `Geometry`. The field is applied for $0 \le z < L$ and only inside the
`APERTURE`. Although the inherited help text mentions integrated strengths
for `L = 0`, a zero-length `MULTIPOLE` has no field.

### `QUADRUPOLE`

The parser-side `OpalQuadrupole` (`src/Elements/OpalQuadrupole.cpp`) creates
the same `MultipoleRep` as `MULTIPOLE`, but takes scalar attributes:

- `K1`, `DK1`: normal quadrupole strength and error
- `K1S`, `DK1S`: skew quadrupole strength and error

They are stored as
$$
\texttt{KN} = \{0, K_1\},\qquad
\texttt{KS} = \{0, K_{1s}\},
$$
with the errors added in the same way as for `MULTIPOLE`.

### Sextupole and higher orders

A sextupole is a `MULTIPOLE` with
$$
\texttt{KN} = \{0, 0, K_2\},\qquad
\texttt{KS} = \{0, 0, K_{2s}\},
$$
and octupole and decapole terms follow at indices 3 and 4.

A `MULTIPOLE` with terms above the quadrupole cannot be used with the
[boundary refinement](../../user-guide/tracking.qmd#ring-boundary-refinement)
of analytic `RING` tracking.

### Class structure

The current parser-side and runtime-side structure is shown below.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-elements-multipole-class-diagram
%%| fig-cap: "Parser-side and runtime-side class structure for the current `MULTIPOLE` and `QUADRUPOLE` implementation."
classDiagram
  direction TB

  class OpalElement
  class OpalMultipole {
    +clone(name)
    +print(os)
    +update()
  }
  class OpalQuadrupole {
    +clone(name)
    +print(os)
    +update()
  }

  class ElementBase
  class Multipole {
    +setNormalComponent(n, v, vError)
    +setSkewComponent(n, v, vError)
    +apply(pc)
    +computeField(R, B, normal, skew, maxNormal, maxSkew)
  }

  class MultipoleRep {
    +clone()
    +getChannel(key)
    +getGeometry()
  }

  class Geometry

  OpalElement <|-- OpalMultipole
  OpalElement <|-- OpalQuadrupole

  ElementBase <|-- Multipole
  Multipole <|-- MultipoleRep

  OpalMultipole ..> MultipoleRep : creates/configures
  OpalQuadrupole ..> MultipoleRep : creates/configures

  MultipoleRep *-- Geometry : geometry
```
